how_built: Merged from nine reader reports (site research, schedule, estimate-to-payments, documents and AI, people and marketplace, global edition, marketing and assets, changelog, live public surface) and two fact-checker passes. Record real screens from a demo account before publishing.

nz.one_liner: QSME NZ (www.qsme.co.nz) is a web app plus an iPhone app that takes a New Zealand build from a public address check to a priced schedule of quantities, tenders, signed agreements, a Gantt programme, site sign-in, milestone payment records and the CCC document pack, all in one project record.
positioning_quotes: Watch your project come to life.
From feasibility to Code Compliance — one place for developers and property owners to plan, price and deliver every New Zealand project.
Built for New Zealand developers & property owners
today: Front door: the homepage address check is public. It shows the LINZ boundary, land area, legal description and council for any NZ address; the planning zone for Auckland, Wellington City, Christchurch and Hamilton only; services and flood/hazard chips for Auckland only. A free account unlocks Site research (verdict, overlays, requirements, feasibility calculator, Pro view, one-page report). Full depth is Auckland only.

Price it: a schedule of quantities (pockets, jobs, lines) filled by typing, Excel/CSV import, templates, or AI drafts that a person checks. 'Read my plans' splits a consent-pack PDF into sections and the AI chat labels where each number came from (paid plan or trial; chat is tagged Beta).

Tender it: private or public tenders cut from a pocket. Bidders never see your rates or budget. Emailed PDF quotes can be read into a checked draft and join the comparison. Bids are compared as totals excluding and including GST with a 'Lowest' tag; each bid opens to its own lines.

Agree it: award creates the payment contract with milestones and retention. Agreements are signed from a link with no account, with a certificate page. 'Make the agreement' writes one from an awarded job as a draft.

Programme it: a Gantt with linked tasks, booked tradies asked before their dates move, rain days, NZ public holidays, a default Christmas shutdown (23 Dec to 11 Jan), 'What drives the finish date', and a printable A4 'Construction programme' on your letterhead.

Run the site: a QR poster on the gate for sign-in with no app or account, a printable register, an induction and daily safety check for tradies, a daily log that writes some entries itself, and project chat.
Pay: milestones are settled 'outside QSME' and confirmed by the receiver (live). NZ open banking is built but not confirmed switched on in production. QSME never holds money; there is no escrow.
Hand over: trade certificates and a CCC pack zip (paid plan); QS reports including a drawdown certificate and cost to complete (paid plan; generated by the user, not certified by a QS).

Marketplace layer (NZ only): public tender board, tradie and supplier directories, products marketplace and property listings are real but nearly empty today: 2 open tenders, 2 public projects, 22 directory profiles (1 verified, 0 ratings), 3 marketplace listings, 0 suppliers in Find a Supplier, 0 property listings.

Money model: free plan (first project free; tradies bid free per the pricing page), paid plans quoted not published, and one fixed fee: 1% each side, capped at $2,000, only when the public marketplace found the work, invoiced when the job completes.

Mobile: iOS app v1.0.0 on the App Store since 23 Sep 2026, sign-in only, 0 ratings. Not on Google Play. Phone features merged after the store build (Site search, Pro cards) are not confirmed in users' hands.

global.one_liner: QSME Global is the same platform for construction organisations outside New Zealand: a demo-led marketing site at qsme.build (15 languages) and the app at app.qsme.build, focused on estimating, private tendering, award into contract, the programme and site records.
positioning_quotes: Tendering and estimating software for construction organisations
It keeps one record per project, and makes the estimate the document that is tendered, contracted and built against — so what was priced, what was agreed and what was done are the same thing.
In production in New Zealand at qsme.co.nz
today: Doors: qsme.build is the marketing site (Book a demo is the call to action; there is no sign-in link). app.qsme.build goes straight to sign-in; self-serve sign-up with a country picker exists but is not linked from qsme.build. Same codebase, backend and database as NZ; what a person sees is decided by their organisation's market and country.

What a global organisation gets: schedule of quantities with AI drafting and Excel import; private, invitation-only tenders (30-day invitations); emailed quotes in the comparison; bids compared on the same tax basis; award into contract with milestones; e-signed agreements; Gantt with linked tasks, finish-date chain, rain days and a printable programme; QR gate sign-in, daily log and chat; documents and plan reading; money recorded, never moved (paid outside, receiver confirms); the AI assistant connector.
What it does not get: site research, the public tender board, tradie/supplier directories, marketplace, property listings, bank payments, success fee, NZBN/LBP checks, the CCC pack and certificates.

Gaps to respect: no public-holiday calendar outside NZ (Monday to Friday only, and the NZ Christmas shutdown is on by default); the organisation's own tax name shows only on the profile, letterhead and checklist so far (bids and contracts still say GST); built-in agreement templates are written for NZ law; the app UI is English, Spanish and Arabic (the 15 languages are the website); team seats, white-label and an embeddable tender board are 'ask sales', not available.

Pricing: per organisation, by the projects running at once; no per-seat fees, no success fee, invited bidders never pay to bid; every plan is quoted by sales in writing. No public price, no free plan or trial is advertised.

Trust posture: the security page states QSME is not ISO 27001 certified (programme in progress), has no SOC 2 report and makes no SSO/MFA claims. There are no customer logos, testimonials or usage numbers anywhere.

1% of contract value each side, capped at NZ$2,000 each side, only when QSME's public marketplace introduced the parties, invoiced when the job completes on QSME's own invoice, never taken out of a payment. No fee when you invited the winner, on a direct contract, when the winner has no account, or when the work ends in a dispute.

Construction Contracts Act 2002 (glossary and the 'Subcontract agreement (NZ)' template: payment claims, schedules, retentions held on trust, adjudication); Contract and Commercial Law Act 2017 (e-signature basis); Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (site induction). None of it is legal advice.

Checklist steps and the CCC pack use real NZ items: PIM, resource and building consent printed on site, SSSP, development contributions, council hold-point inspections, LBP Records of Work, Energy Work Certificates, PS1–PS4, CCC applied for (Form 6), Compliance Schedule and BWoF, defects period. Four NZ checklist templates. CCC pack and certificate registry are NZ only and paid.

12 region pages for tenders, projects and tradies: Auckland, Wellington, Canterbury, Waikato, Bay of Plenty, Otago, Northland, Manawatū-Whanganui, Hawke's Bay, Taranaki, Nelson & Tasman, Southland. Only Auckland has content today.

tradie, subbie, section, consent pack, Gib stopping, LIM, CCC, LBP, council, drainlayer, Aotearoa, whānau, 'Sweet as'. Day-first dates, en-NZ formats ('Mon 12 Oct', 'today 2:14pm'), NZ time on the server. Macrons survive in imports and PDFs ('Kōwhai' once printed as 'K.whai' — fixed). Tutorial voiceovers pronounce the brand 'Q S me'.
NZ real-estate agency work is a licensed activity; QSME's agent mode is a self-serve toggle with no licence check. Needs the owner's legal sign-off before any marketing.

Baqshi Limited trading as QSME®; footer says 'QSME® is a registered trademark of Baqshi Limited' (registration status unconfirmed — the August shareholder report said pending). hello@qsme.co.nz, +64 27 338 8500 (mobile), +64 9 920 8896 (office), Mon–Fri 8am–6pm NZT. Hosts: www.qsme.co.nz (web), api.qsme.co.nz (API).

site_research and nz_address_lookup (by country NZ); find_tradies, public_tenders, bank_payments, nzbn_verification, nz_compliance, marketplace_products, real_estate_listings (by market NZ). All hidden and refused (403) for global organisations.

global_specifics.fact: Marketing site qsme.build (Astro on Cloudflare, no login link, call to action 'Book a demo'); app at app.qsme.build (/ → sign-in, noindex; NZ-only pages redirect to qsme.build). One codebase, backend (api.qsme.co.nz) and database with NZ.

'Book a demo' / 'Talk to sales'. Self-serve sign-up exists at app.qsme.build/sign-up but qsme.build does not link to it (APP_URL empty). Choosing New Zealand on global sign-up sends the person to www.qsme.co.nz.

Website: 15 — English, Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), Spanish, French, Russian, German, Portuguese, Turkish, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Persian; Arabic and Persian right-to-left; Spanish module/solution pages still English; legal pages and the blog English only. App UI: English, Spanish, Arabic. Tutorial videos: English, NZ edition.

198-country table (currency, timezone, dial code); 64 carry a national tax label and rate. No country packs beyond NZ: one Australian residential template, two general templates. Integration-tested sign-up example: Canada → CAD, Toronto, GST 5%. A fixed bug once recommended NZ templates to a Lebanese project.

Site research and LINZ lookups, public tender board and Opportunities browse, tradie and supplier directories, marketplace and products, property listings, NZBN/LBP verification, certificate registry and CCC pack, NZ process templates by default, open-banking payments, success-fee copy. Messaging search is limited to the organisation's own market or existing connections.
Always private, by invitation (30-day invitations, owner-only share link). A tender or project marked public by a global organisation is stored private. No embeddable tender board yet.

'Recorded, never moved': the payer marks a milestone paid outside QSME with a reference and receipt, the receiver confirms. Bank-payment routes answer 403. No success fee is ever accrued for a non-NZ organisation.

Owners can rename the tax (e.g. VAT 20%), but only the profile, letterhead preview and checklist follow it so far; bids, contracts and the comparison still read GST. Letterhead shows 'Reg. no.' instead of NZBN.

No public-holiday calendar outside NZ: projects work Monday to Friday ('No public holidays'). The NZ Christmas shutdown (23 Dec–11 Jan) is still on by default and must be switched off or changed per project.

global_specifics.topic: NZ leftovers inside the global app
global_specifics.fact: Built-in agreement templates are NZ-law ('Subcontract agreement (NZ)'); the AI chat prompt defaults to NZ terms and NZD for non-Australian projects; the AI connector assumes NZD; QS reports print NZIQS; the site sign-in page footer says 'the platform New Zealand builders run their projects on'; the app.qsme.build page title says 'NZ Construction Platform'.

Business / Enterprise / Enterprise + White-label, priced per organisation by projects running at once (open in the same month); no per-seat fees; no success fee; invited bidders never pay; Business month to month, Enterprise annual invoiced; every plan quoted by sales in writing; no public prices, free plan or trial advertised.
Organisation accounts with roles, white-label branding and domain, and the embeddable tender board are not generally available (member management flag off; embed not built).

TLS and HSTS; encrypted daily backups with a key outside the host and a second-location copy; project roles; bidder visibility enforced server-side; signed records kept. Not ISO 27001 certified (programme in progress); no SOC 2; no SSO/MFA claims; hosting region 'confirmed with sales'; DPA and sub-processor list on request.
The iOS app is linked from qsme.build ('Companion iOS app on the App Store') but the build defaults to the NZ market and has not been adapted to read edition settings. No Android.

No customers, logos, testimonials or usage numbers. qsme.build/public/screenshots is empty; every 'screenshot' on the site is an illustration with invented data ('Riverside Terraces — Stage 2'). Embedded walkthroughs are 'Recorded in the New Zealand edition' and show NZD, GST and app.qsme.co.nz.

global_specifics.topic: Words to avoid in global videos
global_specifics.fact: The qsme.build build check bans NZ terms outside About/Contact/Legal: CCC, LBP, tradie, open banking, public tenders, .co.nz addresses, NZ pricing. Say 'drawing set' not 'consent pack', 'tax' not 'GST', 'subcontractor' not 'tradie'.

Baqshi Limited trading as QSME, a New Zealand company; sales phone +64 9 920 8896 (shown as New Zealand); hello@qsme.co.nz (hello@qsme.build not live); reply promise 'within two business days' still marked for the owner to confirm; founder described as 'a professional quantity surveyor and software architect' with no name.
An uncommitted homepage redesign sits in the local qsme.build checkout (bento modules, floating 'Bid received' chips). Screen recordings of the live site taken now may look different later.

story_seeds.title: The strip the council wants
story_seeds.seed: A live test on a small Auckland mixed-use site came back 'Strong development potential' — and, under Constraints, 'Designation · Road Widening (Auckland Transport)'. 'I nearly bought it. Then one line showed the council wants a strip of it for the road.'
story_seeds.guardrail: Auckland address; fictional buyer; indicative only.

story_seeds.title: The back corner
story_seeds.seed: Open home: the front of the section looks dry; the homepage check flips one chip amber — 'Flood plain — Present — check' — because hazards are checked against the whole parcel, not the letterbox.
story_seeds.guardrail: Auckland only; 'Clear' never means 'won't flood'.

story_seeds.title: Room for 3!
story_seeds.seed: The flyer says 'room for 3!'. The code comment says 'Three homes on a 200 m² site aren't real'. The section vs the flyer.
story_seeds.guardrail: Humour at the situation, never at an agent or customer; 'indicatively'.

story_seeds.title: Just a deck
story_seeds.seed: A homeowner planning a deck finds 'On a cross-lease the other flat owners must consent to any change of footprint'. Now they need the neighbour's signature.
story_seeds.guardrail: Punch at the situation, not the neighbour.

story_seeds.title: The dream garage on a sewer main
story_seeds.seed: 'A public wastewater pipe crosses or borders the site: building within its clearance needs … approval, a CCTV survey and often a pipe relocation.'
story_seeds.guardrail: Auckland; pipe positions approximate.

story_seeds.title: The zone says five storeys; the maunga says no
story_seeds.seed: 'A viewshaft can cap height below the zone figure — the storeys above are not guaranteed.' Very Auckland.
story_seeds.guardrail: Auckland only.

story_seeds.title: The villa you planned to bowl
story_seeds.seed: 'Special character rules usually mean keeping the existing house, which lowers the realistic yield.'
story_seeds.guardrail: Auckland only.

story_seeds.title: Run the number in the car
story_seeds.seed: Anti-FOMO auction story: in the car park before bidding, type the sale price and see 'What you could pay for the land to keep a 20% margin'.
story_seeds.guardrail: Label 'illustrative numbers'; not financial advice; user's own inputs.

story_seeds.title: The big back yard
story_seeds.seed: The checklist surfaces 'Granny flat without consent … up to 70 m²' on low-density zones — parents in the backyard, keys sooner.
story_seeds.guardrail: Keep 'can often… where the site meets the conditions'.

story_seeds.title: Cheap for a reason
story_seeds.seed: No wastewater main near the lifestyle block: 'budget for a network extension (often via neighbouring land, needing easements) or an on-site system'.
story_seeds.guardrail: Auckland region data only.

story_seeds.title: Paste it how you got it
story_seeds.seed: People paste 'Flat 2, 12 Mt Eden Rd, Mount Eden, Auckland 1024, New Zealand' and most address boxes choke; QSME offers the 'Closest match'. And for a brand-new subdivision: 'Not in the address register yet — that's fine, carry on.'
story_seeds.guardrail: Don't demo '12 mt eden rd' as an exact hit.

story_seeds.title: The tool that tells you to call a planner
story_seeds.seed: Every card ends 'Indicative only… Confirm with a planner or the council.' A video where QSME tells you what to ask the professional you are about to pay.
story_seeds.guardrail: On-brand honesty; no 'replaces a planner'.

story_seeds.title: Section to shovel (long form)
story_seeds.seed: One Auckland address followed through Site research → verdict → requirements → rough feasibility → 'Create project here' → SOQ → tender → programme.
story_seeds.guardrail: Demo project, invented people, Auckland commercial or owner's own address.

story_seeds.title: The 120-page consent pack
story_seeds.seed: Nobody, including the builder, reads it end to end. Press 'Read a document' and watch 'Finding the sections…' become '4 of 11 sections ready'. Then: 'Heads up: no drainage found in this pack.' — before the tender, not on site.
story_seeds.guardrail: Paid plan/trial; say 'drawing set' for Global; it reads, it does not measure.

story_seeds.title: A guess dressed up as a fact
story_seeds.seed: A generic chatbot gives a confident number; QSME's chat labels it 'My estimate' and the drawing answer 'From your documents (… p.12)'.
story_seeds.guardrail: Show the Beta line; never claim it is always right.

story_seeds.title: Which one's cheapest?
story_seeds.seed: One quote says '8,298 incl.', one '7,400 + GST', a sole trader's flat '7,900'. Flip 'Compare on' and the 'Lowest' tag moves. 'Because “2,000” means two different amounts to a client and a GST-registered builder — $300 apart on a $2,000 job.'
story_seeds.guardrail: NZ GST; for Global say 'same tax basis' and check labels.

story_seeds.title: The subbie who only sends PDFs
story_seeds.seed: 'A subcontractor who quotes by PDF is not lost.' Drop the PDF in; QSME flags that the lines don't add up to the total; tick it against the original and it sits in the same table.
story_seeds.guardrail: Owner checks every figure; do not name the retailer from the commit example.

story_seeds.title: Five lump sums
story_seeds.seed: 'Five lump sums that cannot be held against each other' vs every bidder pricing the same SOQ lines.
story_seeds.guardrail: Comparison is totals plus each bid's own lines, not a cross-bid matrix.

story_seeds.title: Your budget stays yours
story_seeds.seed: Split screen: owner's lines with rates and budget; bidder's same lines with the rate column empty. 'Rates, amounts and the tender budget are stripped out server-side, not hidden in the interface.'

story_seeds.title: What is actually holding this build up?
story_seeds.seed: 'The one question a lender asks — what is actually holding this build up? — had no answer on the page.' An A4 programme slides across a desk: purple-ringed tasks and 'Any one of them running late moves the whole finish.'
story_seeds.guardrail: No bank names; never 'bank-approved'.

story_seeds.title: $450k that read as $2.7m
story_seeds.seed: A spreadsheet programme repeats a $450,000 contract price on six rows; QSME prints it once.

story_seeds.title: The January lie
story_seeds.seed: A developer promises a mid-January handover; the programme counted 24 Dec–10 Jan as working days and 'finished about two weeks earlier on paper than it ever could in life'. Fix on screen: '12 jobs are planned on days the site is shut' → 'Move them off the days off'.
story_seeds.guardrail: Old programmes only move when the button is pressed.

story_seeds.title: The Labour Day pour
story_seeds.seed: 'A concrete pour does not care that it is Labour Day' — one switch lets that one task work that one holiday.
story_seeds.guardrail: No regional anniversary days in the calendar.

story_seeds.title: Asked, not told
story_seeds.seed: Group-text chaos vs one amber card: 'New dates — can you make them?' → 'Can't make it — On another site until the 20th'. 'A task with someone booked on it is never moved on them.'
story_seeds.guardrail: In-app and email only (no SMS); people not on QSME get 'Give them a ring'.

story_seeds.title: 'Dates saved' — the lie software tells
story_seeds.seed: A refused drag used to vanish while the toast said 'Dates saved'. Now: 'Gib stayed on Mon 12 Oct — it can't start before Framing finishes'.
story_seeds.guardrail: Self-deprecating; owner sign-off for internal-bug stories.

story_seeds.title: Rained off, again
story_seeds.seed: Tick a whole washed-out week in one go, preview what moves, 'Push these tasks'; the history says 'Rain day' as the reason.
story_seeds.guardrail: A person logs the rain day; the forecast only shades the chart.

story_seeds.title: Written for somebody who has not built before
story_seeds.seed: Template notes: 'Frames that arrive early sit in the rain; frames that arrive late stop the whole job.' / 'one tile on a slow boat holds up four bathrooms.' / connections are 'the biggest hidden risk… apply in week one'.
story_seeds.guardrail: Durations are estimates.

story_seeds.title: Deal done on the phone
story_seeds.seed: 'A builder puts the task on the programme first and does the deal after, on the phone' — and used to get a second bar. Now the award lands on the same task.

story_seeds.title: Agreed in every sense except a signature
story_seeds.seed: 'An awarded job was already an agreement in every sense except that nobody ever signed anything.' Amber banner → 'Make the agreement' → signed on a phone in the ute, no account.
story_seeds.guardrail: Draft first, nothing sent automatically; NZ-law templates.

story_seeds.title: The same squiggle, redrawn with a mouse
story_seeds.seed: 'A builder signs their own subcontracts, variations and letters of intent — the same squiggle, redrawn with a mouse on every one of them.' → one kept signature.

story_seeds.title: 'I paid you last week'
story_seeds.seed: Only the payer can mark it paid, only the receiver can confirm, and one person cannot be both. 'Marking something paid that you have not paid is the one thing the screen warns you about.'
story_seeds.guardrail: QSME does not verify outside payments; never 'release the funds'.

story_seeds.title: The clipboard at the gate
story_seeds.seed: A wet, half-empty sign-in book vs a laminated poster: 'Print it, laminate it, cable-tie it to the fence.' Gloves on: the whole row is the tap target. Later: 'Who was on site that day?' — the register on the builder's letterhead.
story_seeds.guardrail: No compliance claims; invented names on the register.

story_seeds.title: The diary that writes itself
story_seeds.seed: 'A rain day — the single biggest thing that happens to a build — left no mark at all.' Now it writes itself into the daily log.
story_seeds.guardrail: Only some entries write themselves.

story_seeds.title: The group text nobody can find
story_seeds.seed: 'Chat tied to the job, not a group text that nobody can find in six months.' The seeded plasterer thread ends 'Sweet as, see you Thursday.'
story_seeds.guardrail: No in-app calls; do not film the call button.

story_seeds.title: Everyone filed under 'Contractor'
story_seeds.seed: 21 of 52 contacts under 'Contractor' because there was nowhere to put a drainlayer or a scaffolder. 'Name it the way you say it on site.'
story_seeds.guardrail: Use generically; don't cite the account.

story_seeds.title: It just does the typing
story_seeds.seed: On the couch: 'What's on my schedule this week, and who's turning up?' then 'Draft a tender for the plumbing and drainage jobs'. Cut to QSME, where a person presses publish. 'If an assistant tells you it has sent, paid or awarded something, it has not.'
story_seeds.guardrail: No vendor endorsement; paid ChatGPT plan needed.

story_seeds.title: The Friday payment tracker
story_seeds.seed: 'Here is my payment tracker — put it in QSME as a sheet, then tell me what is still unpaid.'
story_seeds.guardrail: A sheet only records; marking Paid pays nobody.

story_seeds.title: The shoebox of certificates
story_seeds.seed: Chasing Records of Work and electrical certificates at the end of a build vs one CCC Pack zip.
story_seeds.guardrail: QSME compiles; it does not issue or lodge; paid plan.

story_seeds.title: Not found in a Facebook group
story_seeds.seed: Homeowner scrolling a community group for a builder vs sending one scope to invited trades — 'invited to your project, not found in a Facebook group'.
story_seeds.guardrail: Do not say the directory is verified (1 of 22).

story_seeds.title: Your own crew is always free
story_seeds.seed: A tradie sceptical of lead-gen fees hears: 'We don't take a cut of work you found yourself.' The fee is 1% each side, capped at $2,000, only when the public marketplace found the work.
story_seeds.guardrail: No plan prices; bid-cost conflict unresolved.

story_seeds.title: Handed another country's checklist
story_seeds.seed: 'A Lebanese project was being recommended NZ templates.' The moment software assumes you live somewhere else — and the fix: the project's country first, then 'General — any country'.
story_seeds.guardrail: Owner sign-off for internal-bug stories.

story_seeds.title: Vocabulary is where trust starts
story_seeds.seed: The same bid table while the word changes: Leistungsverzeichnis, 工程量清单, جدول الكميات, poz poz. 'Yours next — tell us.'
story_seeds.guardrail: The website is in 15 languages; the app is in 3.

story_seeds.title: 'Is QSME ISO 27001 certified? No.'
story_seeds.seed: A procurement manager braced for a sales pitch gets a one-word honest answer. 'We do not display badges, logos or ratings we have not earned.'
story_seeds.guardrail: Quote the page exactly.

story_seeds.title: Why is there no price list?
story_seeds.seed: 'You get a price by email, not a call you did not ask for.' Per organisation, by projects running at once; no per-seat fee; subcontractors never pay to bid.
story_seeds.guardrail: No prices.

story_seeds.title: The wrong door
story_seeds.seed: Someone in New Zealand lands on the global sign-up, picks New Zealand, and is politely walked across: 'New Zealand has its own edition of QSME.'

story_seeds.title: Think before every phone buzzes
story_seeds.seed: 'Nothing goes out to the trades while you re-plan.' Flip to Private, re-plan, flip back.
story_seeds.guardrail: Public link shows money by default.

story_seeds.title: $1,250.50 became $125,050
story_seeds.seed: A real bug, fixed before launch: 'A bid of $1,250.50 was submitted as $125,050.' 'We sweat the cents' — punching at ourselves.
story_seeds.guardrail: Owner sign-off required before using internal-bug stories.

red_list.claim: Escrow, 'held in trust', 'we hold your money', 'funds released on approval', payment protection, guaranteed or 'secure' payments
red_list.why: QSME never holds money; escrow was withdrawn and has no routes. Reserved words until a financial-service licence exists.

red_list.claim: Blockchain, crypto, stablecoins, smart contracts, 'on-chain' anything
red_list.why: Never deployed. Old blog posts and a /support waitlist line still say it — do not repeat.

red_list.claim: 'QSME manages your build', 'we hire the trades for you', 'QSME is your project manager'
red_list.why: The managed option is switched off.

red_list.claim: Any plan price ($9, $99, $499, $999), '50c per credit', or any Global price
red_list.why: Prices are quoted, not published.

red_list.claim: '14-day free trial', 'free forever', 'completely free', 'no fees'
red_list.why: The pricing page says 'No trial clock'; free is one project; the 1% success fee exists. Owner must pick the trial message.

red_list.claim: 'Everyone bids free' / any credit cost for public bids
red_list.why: Pricing page and Knowledge Hub contradict each other; main contractors need GC Pro.

red_list.claim: 'Any NZ address' for zoning, services, hazards, overlays or development potential; nationwide coverage
red_list.why: Zone: 4 councils. Everything deeper: Auckland only. Film Auckland and say 'Auckland first'.

red_list.claim: That site research is a LIM, PIM, title search, valuation, planning advice or council-approved; 'you can build X'; 'no consent needed'; 'flood-free'
red_list.why: Every card says 'Indicative only… not advice'.

red_list.claim: Owner names, CV / land value, sale prices or sales history
red_list.why: Locked placeholders: 'Available with a data licence'.

red_list.claim: 'Verified tradies', 'every trade verified', 'licence-verified directory'; automatic register checks for all licences; police/background checks; instant or free verification
red_list.why: 1 of 22 profiles is verified, 0 have a verified licence; only LBP has an automated lookup (if configured); a verification fee setting exists.

red_list.claim: Any count: users, customers, projects, tenders, tradies, suppliers, listings, downloads, ratings; 'thousands', 'hundreds', 'across the country'
red_list.why: Live numbers are tiny (2 tenders, 2 projects, 22 profiles, 3 listings, 0 properties, 0 app ratings).

red_list.claim: Testimonials, customer logos, case studies, star ratings, or fictional characters presented as real customers
red_list.why: None exist; studio rule forbids fake testimonials.

red_list.claim: Time or money saved ('20 hours a week', 'Save 15–25%'), 'mentor support'
red_list.why: No evidence (old blog and App Store listing).

red_list.claim: A side-by-side line-by-line matrix across bidders; 'QSME picks the winner'; 'conforming bid'
red_list.why: The comparison is a totals table plus each bid's own lines; award is a person's decision.

red_list.claim: Drawing mark-up, circling, takeoff, on-screen measurement; 'AI measures your drawings'
red_list.why: Viewer switched off since 4 Sep; AI reads what drawings say. qsme.build still says 'mark up the drawings'.

red_list.claim: 'Nothing is guessed', '100% accurate AI', 'AI replaces your QS / planner / lawyer'
red_list.why: The chat is Beta and says 'It can get things wrong'; every AI output is a draft to check.

red_list.claim: An AI assistant that awards, signs, pays, publishes a tender, changes the schedule or 'summarises the bids'; an official partnership with Anthropic or OpenAI; works with free ChatGPT
red_list.why: Those tools do not exist on the connection; it is a user-added connector.

red_list.claim: 'Legally binding everywhere', legal advice, lawyer-approved templates, e-signature validity outside NZ
red_list.why: Templates are 'a starting point, not legal advice'; the legal basis cited is NZ law only.

red_list.claim: QS reports or the programme as 'bank-approved', 'bank-ready', 'accepted by lenders', certified by a QS; naming any bank
red_list.why: Generated by the user from their own SOQ; 'a document a bank can be handed' is a commit phrase.

red_list.claim: QSME issues the CCC, producer statements or certificates; guarantees consent or a CCC; lodges with council or sends to a lender
red_list.why: QSME records and compiles; the user downloads and sends.

red_list.claim: Health-and-safety compliance (WorkSafe, HSWA) from sign-in, induction or checklists
red_list.why: 'A record, not a lock'.

red_list.claim: Android / Google Play; SMS or text messages; in-app calls; offline mode; phone features merged after 23 Sep (Site search, Pro cards, native schedule edits) shown as in the app
red_list.why: iOS only; SMS delivery failing; calling removed; store build predates those commits.

red_list.claim: 'The app is in 15 languages'; fully translated Spanish pages; native-reviewed translations
red_list.why: Website: 15; app: English, Spanish, Arabic; Spanish product pages partly English.

red_list.claim: Global: local public holidays, local tax compliance, tax name on every document, data residency, team seats, white-label, embedded tender board, public tender board, directories, marketplace, site research, bank payments
red_list.why: None exist for global organisations.

red_list.claim: NZ words in Global videos: tradie, CCC, LBP, open banking, public tenders, GST, consent pack, NZD
red_list.why: Banned by the qsme.build copy rules; use subcontractor, tax, drawing set.

red_list.claim: ISO 27001 certified / compliant / audited / 'by <date>'; SOC 2; SSO; MFA; GDPR-compliant; pen-tested; bank-grade or military-grade
red_list.why: The security page explicitly says not certified and makes no such claims.

red_list.claim: Removed features: Book a tradie, Quick Jobs, Bookings, tradie Quotes & Variations, invoice builder, CRM pipeline, calling/screen share, percent-complete
red_list.why: All removed; still visible in old clips and screenshots.

red_list.claim: Properties to browse, licensed/verified agents, commission terms, investment returns, 'real-estate portal'
red_list.why: 0 listings; agent mode is self-declared with no licence check.

red_list.claim: Buying, ordering, checkout or delivery in the marketplace; a stocked catalogue
red_list.why: Catalogue only, 3 listings.

red_list.claim: 'The public schedule link never shows money'
red_list.why: Money on the public page is ON by default.

red_list.claim: Variations that change the contract sum; cash-flow forecasting; rate book; estimate version history; accounting software / replaces Xero or MYOB
red_list.why: Unmerged branches or not built.

red_list.claim: QSME holds, protects or releases retention; retention-trust compliance
red_list.why: Retention is a recorded percentage; no release workflow.

red_list.claim: Named competitors or comparisons (Procore, Buildertrend, Buildxact, Builderscrack, Relab, CoreLogic, QV, homes.co.nz, Trade Me Property, OneRoof)
red_list.why: QSME does not win on breadth; old comparison blog was judged inaccurate.

red_list.claim: Walkthrough videos as screen recordings, real footage or a real person's voice; reusing payments/awarded-work audio ('release the funds', 'platform fee')
red_list.why: Remotion animations with an AI voice; some lines are now wrong.

red_list.claim: Template durations as official ('your townhouses will take 10¾ months')
red_list.why: Estimates from one automated web pass; numbers differ between sources.

red_list.claim: 'Sign up at qsme.build' / 'Sign up free' as the Global call to action
red_list.why: qsme.build is demo-led and has no sign-up link.

red_list.claim: 'Instant' site research, verification or plan reading
red_list.why: Seconds to minutes; verification usually one business day.

red_list.claim: 'Registered trademark' spoken on camera
red_list.why: Footer says registered; the August shareholder report said pending — confirm first.

red_list.claim: Internal material: audit findings, shareholder numbers, commit counts, App Store rejection history, backup incidents, the 'CEO's first file' story
red_list.why: Confidential or needs owner sign-off.

red_list.claim: Real private addresses, names, emails, phone numbers, registers or tokens on screen
red_list.why: Privacy; studio rules. Use a demo project and invented people.

red_list.claim: Old App Store wording: 'Have a site? Enter the address to see what's possible', 'FREE FOR CLIENTS & TRADIES', '14 relevant tenders of 15'
red_list.why: Retired or demo data.

open_questions.question: Has a real milestone been paid through NZ open banking in production?
open_questions.why: The fact-checker downgraded it to merged; it depends on production config. No payment video until confirmed.

open_questions.question: Which trial message do we use: the in-app '14-day free trial' or the pricing page's 'No trial clock' / 'Free is a plan, not a trial'?
open_questions.why: Both are live and read as a contradiction.

open_questions.question: Do public-tender bids cost anything? Pricing page: 'Bid free, forever'. Tenders guide: 'Charged in wallet credits', monthly allowance, GC Pro to bid. Code: 0.
open_questions.why: Every tradie-side video depends on it; the guide should be fixed either way.

open_questions.question: What can we say about verification? Is the MBIE LBP key set, is the automated ID scan on, is there a verification fee — and will the homepage line 'Every trade. Verified.' be changed (1 of 22 verified)?
open_questions.why: 'Verified' is the riskiest word on the live site.

open_questions.question: Privacy: the public profiles endpoint (no login) returns an email for 14 of 22 profiles, a phone for 3, plus wallet_address and subscription_plan. Intended, or a leak?
open_questions.why: Possible exposure of members' contact details; fix before driving traffic.

open_questions.question: Is phone Site search (and the later phone schedule changes) in users' hands via an over-the-air update? When will SMS delivery be fixed? Any Android date?
open_questions.why: Phone UGC (open-home scenes) depends on it.

open_questions.question: Who records real screens from a demo account (NZ and Global) with invented people, a letterhead, a sample programme PDF — and which address may be shown?
open_questions.why: No current screenshots exist; nobody logged in during research.

open_questions.question: Global call to action: 'Book a demo' or app.qsme.build/sign-up? What plan does a self-signed-up organisation get?
open_questions.why: qsme.build has no sign-in link; sign-up is live but hidden.

open_questions.question: Are the 2 public tenders and 2 public projects demo seed data? May they appear on screen?
open_questions.why: At least one tender came from the App Store reviewer seed script.

open_questions.question: Real-estate agent mode: legal sign-off on marketing to agents without a licence check, and is there a commission?
open_questions.why: Licensed activity in NZ.

open_questions.question: Will stale public copy be fixed before videos drive traffic? Blog posts (escrow, on-chain, '20 hours a week', competitor tables), /support 'on-chain' waitlist, qsme.build 'mark up the drawings' and 'summarise the bids', Knowledge Hub 'two of ours' templates and 'one timeline'.
open_questions.why: Viewers will land on pages that contradict the videos.

open_questions.question: Is Wellington zoning reliable, and is the owner comfortable showing non-Auckland yield numbers (a Christchurch point returned 70–175 homes)?
open_questions.why: Determines whether any non-Auckland demo is safe.

open_questions.question: The helper text says '12 mt eden rd' finds 12 Mount Eden Road, but live it returns only 'Closest match' rows. Copy bug or ranking bug?
open_questions.why: Pick a different demo address either way.

open_questions.question: Global: is it intended that non-NZ projects get the NZ Christmas shutdown by default, NZ-law agreement templates, 'GST' on bids, NZ wording in the AI chat and connector, NZIQS on QS reports, and an NZ footer on the sign-in page?
open_questions.why: Decides which features can appear in Global videos.

open_questions.question: Will the July/September walkthrough videos be re-rendered? Do the ElevenLabs voice and music licences cover paid social? Is 'Recorded in the New Zealand edition' acceptable wording for animations?
open_questions.why: They are the only ready-made footage.

open_questions.question: May internal honesty stories be used publicly ('Dates saved' bug, the $1,250.50 bid bug, the council pack that was refused, the contact-import bugs, the Lebanese-template bug)?
open_questions.why: Strong self-deprecating content, but they disclose internal incidents.

open_questions.question: Is QSME® registered or pending?
open_questions.why: Footer and shareholder report disagree.

open_questions.question: Free plan reality: one project (pricing page) or three (App Store review notes)? AI allowance lifetime (code) or monthly (Knowledge Hub)?
open_questions.why: Any 'free' script needs the right limits.

open_questions.question: Is there a Dispute button users can reach? How is retention release shown, and which wording — 'released at warranty', 'end of the defects period' or 'completion'?
open_questions.why: API exists without UI; three wordings exist.

open_questions.question: Townhouses template: quote 136 tasks / 235 working days (current file) or 140 / 185 (original commit) — or neither?
open_questions.why: Sources disagree.

open_questions.question: Is any licence for owner names, CV or sales data planned?
open_questions.why: Only placeholders exist.

open_questions.question: Should screen recording wait for the shorter sidebar, new colour themes and the uncommitted qsme.build redesign to ship?
open_questions.why: Videos recorded now may date quickly.

open_questions.question: Fix sitemaps (profiles empty, geo Auckland only) and server-render /properties and /marketplace before driving traffic?
open_questions.why: SEO and first-visit experience.

open_questions.question: Will the App Store listing description be corrected ('Save 15–25%', 'mentor support', 'Automated Bill of Quantities', 'Secure Progress Payments')?
open_questions.why: Viewers sent to the listing will read claims the videos avoid.
